skill.name: skill-creator
skill.description: Guide for creating or updating AI skills with structured planning, reusable resources, validation, packaging, and iteration across Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
skill.summary: Guides teams through designing, validating, and packaging reusable AI skills.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline code examples, and template strings containing backticks; no Ruby or shell backtick execution was found. The archive code supports legitimate packaging, but it recursively includes every file under the skill folder and can disclose hidden files or secrets. No prompt injection language was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The package script recursively includes every file in the skill folder.
remediation.suggestion: Add denylist or allowlist filtering for .env files, .git data, caches, archives, credentials, and unrelated local artifacts before creating the zip.

remediation.issue: The initializer creates placeholder resource files that may remain in finished skills.
remediation.suggestion: Make validation warn when placeholder examples remain, or require authors to confirm they intentionally kept each generated resource.

semantic_findings.title: Packaging May Include Unintended Files
semantic_findings.description: The packaging script walks every file under the selected skill directory and writes each one into the archive. It does not exclude hidden files, credentials, caches, or unrelated local artifacts before distribution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code uses rglob('*') and writes every file to the zip, so the disclosure risk is direct. The risk depends on local folder contents, so medium severity is appropriate.

content.value_statement: Building reusable AI skills is hard to structure consistently. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through planning, scaffolding, validation, packaging, and iteration.
actual_capabilities: Explains required SKILL.md frontmatter and body structure.
Describes when to use scripts, references, and assets.
Provides a Python initializer for template skill folders.
Validates frontmatter, naming rules, and description format.
Packages validated skill folders into distributable zip archives.
Guides iteration after real usage feedback.
limitations: Does not create domain-specific resources without user input.
The validator performs basic structural checks only.
The initializer writes placeholder examples that require review.
The package script does not filter hidden files or secrets.

use_cases.title: Create a new team skill
use_cases.description: Plan the skill purpose, create a starter folder, and fill SKILL.md with concise operating guidance.

use_cases.title: Standardize reusable workflows
use_cases.description: Convert repeated agent work into scripts, references, assets, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Prepare skills for sharing
use_cases.description: Validate folder structure, package the skill, and review placeholder resources before distribution.

prompt_templates.title: Start a New Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple reusable skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new skill for release note drafting. Ask only for essential missing details, then scaffold the skill and explain what to edit.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Skill Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these example user requests and decide which scripts, references, or assets this skill should include. Keep SKILL.md concise.

prompt_templates.title: Validate an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate maintenance of a local skill folder.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this skill folder, run the validator, fix structural issues, and report any placeholder resources that should be removed.

prompt_templates.title: Refine for Publication
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced preparation for sharing a mature skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this skill for marketplace publication. Check trigger clarity, resource organization, validation results, packaging readiness, and security-sensitive files.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for writing customer support macros.
output_examples.output: A concise skill plan with trigger guidance, suggested references, validation steps, and a starter folder ready for editing.

output_examples.input: Validate and package my finished analytics skill.
output_examples.output: A validation result, packaging status, files included in the archive, and issues to fix before sharing.

output_examples.input: Improve this existing skill after several failed uses.
output_examples.output: A focused revision plan that tightens instructions, removes unused resources, and adds checks based on observed failures.

best_practices: Define clear trigger conditions in the description before adding resources.
Keep SKILL.md concise and move long references into separate files.
Validate generated folders before packaging or sharing them.
anti_patterns: Leaving placeholder scripts or reference files in a finished skill.
Putting large reference material directly in SKILL.md.
Packaging directories that contain credentials, private notes, or unrelated files.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create reusable AI skills with SKILL.md instructions, optional resources, validation, and packaging.

faq.question: Does it work with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it generate a starter skill folder?
faq.answer: Yes. The included initializer creates a template skill folder with example resources.

faq.question: Does it validate completed skills?
faq.answer: Yes. The validator checks required frontmatter, naming rules, and simple description constraints.

faq.question: Can it package skills for distribution?
faq.answer: Yes. The package script validates the folder and creates a zip archive.

faq.question: What should users review before packaging?
faq.answer: Users should remove placeholders, hidden files, credentials, caches, and unrelated local artifacts.
